item.text:
**2B.1 Research Note: Sheikh Hasina in 2024**

Overall read: **mostly negative**. I found a small amount of diplomacy-oriented evidence, but the strongest 2024 record shows Hasina relying on coercion in the student-protest crisis rather than consistently choosing negotiation, compromise, or de-escalation when peaceful options were available.

**Accepted claims**

- **PM Hasina reiterates call to China to help repatriate Rohingyas to Myanmar**
  - **Publisher:** TBS News / UNB
  - **Date:** July 10, 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/pm-hasina-reiterates-call-china-help-repatriate-rohingyas-myanmar-895921
  - **Claim-level summary:** Hasina asked China to help facilitate Rohingya repatriation through discussions with Myanmar. This is the clearest 2024 pro-diplomacy item I found and shows use of a peaceful regional channel rather than force.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.1, 1B.1, 1B.8

- **Student killed amid violent anti-quota protests in Bangladesh**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters / ThePrint
  - **Date:** July 16, 2024
  - **URL:** https://theprint.in/world/student-killed-amid-violent-anti-quota-protests-in-bangladesh/2177010/
  - **Claim-level summary:** Reuters reported that protests continued after Hasina refused to meet student demands, citing ongoing court proceedings, even though the Supreme Court had already suspended the quota order. This shows a credible peaceful route existed, but Hasina did not personally use it as the first response.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.1, 1B.8, 1B.5

- **Bangladesh shuts offices, imposes curfew to curb deadly job quota protests**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters / Investing.com
  - **Date:** July 20, 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-studentled-protests-spiral-3527920
  - **Claim-level summary:** After at least 114 deaths in the protest week, the government closed offices, imposed a curfew, and deployed soldiers. That is strong evidence that force was the preferred crisis tool rather than de-escalation.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.1, 1B.8, 1B.5

- **Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters / Investing.com
  - **Date:** July 22, 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-calm-a-day-after-top-court-scrapped-some-job-quotas-3528153
  - **Claim-level summary:** Hasina kept the curfew in place and blamed political opponents for the violence, saying the curfew would end only when conditions improved. This is escalation and blame-shifting, not compromise.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.1, 1B.8, 1B.5

- **Bangladesh: Türk decries government crackdown, urges respect for international human rights standards**
  - **Publisher:** United Nations / OHCHR
  - **Date:** July 26, 2024
  - **URL:** https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights
  - **Claim-level summary:** The UN said more than 170 people had been killed and warned that internet shutdowns increase impunity. This is strong external confirmation that the state response was coercive and not meaningfully de-escalatory.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.1, 1B.8, 1B.5

- **Exclusive-Bangladesh army refused to suppress protest, sealing Hasina's fate**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters / Investing.com
  - **Date:** August 6, 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/exclusivebangladesh-army-refused-to-suppress-protest-sealing-hasinas-fate-3558302
  - **Claim-level summary:** Reuters reported the army decided not to fire on civilians to enforce the curfew. That implies Hasina was depending on force to control the crisis, and the coercive option only failed because the army refused.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.1, 1B.8, 1B.5

**Synthesis**

- **Positive evidence exists, but it is narrow and indirect**:
  - Rohingya repatriation diplomacy with China.
  - Judicial routing on the quota issue as a nonviolent alternative.
- **Negative evidence is much stronger**:
  - refusal to meet protest demands,
  - curfews,
  - shutdowns,
  - army deployment,
  - blame-shifting,
  - lethal repression.
- Best-supported conclusion: **Hasina did not generally choose diplomacy, compromise, and de-escalation over force in 2024 when peaceful alternatives existed.**
